thread.old_title: Gethsemane Cup Of Suffering And The Sons Substantial Submission To The Father
thread.title: Gethsemane — the cup in the Father's hand, and not as I will, but as thou wilt (Psalm 75; Isaiah 51; John 10; Hebrews 5; Zechariah 13)
thread.old_summary: **`gethsemane-cup-of-suffering-and-the-sons-substantial-submission-to-the-father`** — anchor at Matt 26:36-46. The substantial-Gethsemane substance + the substantial-cup-of-suffering substance per `cup-of-suffering-tanakh-substance` thread (PROPOSED at Matt 20 from S85) + the substantial-Son's-submission-to-the-Father per the Formless-Formed grid per `nature-of-god-formed-in-flesh` thread. Framework rules out Trinitarian-three-co-equal-persons + modalist-collapse + Arian-created-being; the substantial-Son's-eternal-submission preserved in incarnation. 16 members.
thread.summary:
It ain't new. The cup he prayed over in the garden was already in the Father's hand in the Psalms and the prophets, and the prayer itself, not my will but thine, is what the Son had said of himself all along. Matthew sets the scene:

*Then cometh Yahusha (Jesus) with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples, Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder.* (Matthew 26:36)

*Then saith he unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me.* (Matthew 26:38)

*And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.* (Matthew 26:39)

The soul cast down was the psalmist's before it was his:

*Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in Elohim (God): for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.* (Psalm 42:5)

And the cup is not a figure Matthew made up. It is the cup of fury in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), poured out and drunk to the dregs:

*For in the hand of Yahuah (LORD) there is a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture; and he poureth out of the same: but the dregs thereof, all the wicked of the earth shall wring them out, and drink them.* (Psalm 75:8)

*Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of Yahuah (LORD) the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out.* (Isaiah 51:17)

*Thus saith thy Yahuah (Lord) Yahuah (LORD), and thy Elohim (God) that pleadeth the cause of his people, Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again:* (Isaiah 51:22)

Isaiah says the cup is taken out of Jerusalem's hand. In the garden it is put into his. He had already asked the sons of Zebedee whether they could drink it:

*But Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.* (Matthew 20:22)

Luke adds the angel and the sweat:

*Saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.* (Luke 22:42)

*And there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him.* (Luke 22:43)

*And being in an agony he prayed more earnestly: and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.* (Luke 22:44)

Read what the prayer is. It is the Son asking the Father, and the Son's will bending to the Father's will. He is Elohim (God), and he has a Father, and he does the Father's will. He said so before the garden, said it in the garden, and said it from the cross:

*Then answered Yahusha (Jesus) and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.* (John 5:19)

*Now is my soul troubled; and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour: but for this cause came I unto this hour.* (John 12:27)

*And when Yahusha (Jesus) had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.* (Luke 23:46)

Nobody took the life from him. The cup was drunk because he chose to drink it, and the choosing was the Father's commandment kept:

*No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father.* (John 10:18)

Hebrews says plainly what the garden was:

*Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;* (Hebrews 5:7)

*Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;* (Hebrews 5:8)

And Paul says that same mind is the one we are to carry:

*Let this mind be in you, which was also in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus):* (Philippians 2:5)

*And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.* (Philippians 2:8)

Set Abraham beside it. He also rose early and went up the mountain with his only son, and Matthew does not say the word; put the two side by side and read:

*And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.* (Genesis 22:2)

Then the hour comes, the shepherd is struck as Zechariah said, and the sheep run:

*Then cometh he to his disciples, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of Adam is betrayed into the hands of sinners.* (Matthew 26:45)

*Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.* (Zechariah 13:7)

The sheep who scattered that night are the little ones his hand turns toward. They slept while he prayed, and the charge he gave them in the garden is still the charge:

*Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.* (Matthew 26:41)

The garden is another hard place he goes into on purpose. He is brought to both, and in both he does not turn aside. The hour in the garden is not the first time his obedience is tested.

cards.tgt_text: Therefore doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again.
cards.old_note: *No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself.*
cards.note: John 10:17 — *Therefore doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again.* *Then comes Yahusha (Jesus) with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and says unto the disciples, Sit you here, while I go and pray yonder.* (Matthew 26:36) He says the Father loves him because he lays down his life. cards.src_text: Then comes Yahusha (Jesus) with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and says unto the disciples, Sit you here, while I go and pray yonder.
cards.tgt_text: And it came to pass after these things, that Elohim (God) did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.
cards.old_note: The substantial-Aqedat-Yitschaq (binding of Isaac) substance — the substantial-Tanakh-typology.
cards.note: Genesis 22:1 — *And it came to pass after these things, that Elohim (God) did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.* *Then comes Yahusha (Jesus) with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and says unto the disciples, Sit you here, while I go and pray yonder.* (Matthew 26:36) Elohim (God) tests Abraham, and Abraham answers, *Behold, here I am*. The very next word is about taking his son. Set that beside the garden and the two sit together: a father's word, a son going toward it, and an answer that does not argue. Matthew does not say the word. Put the two side by side.

cards.src_text: Saying, Father, if you be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but yours, be done.
cards.tgt_text: And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.
cards.old_note: thread:gethsemane-cup-of-suffering-and-the-sons-substantial-submission-to-the-father | *Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done* (Luke 22:42). The Gethsemane prayer — the Formed-Son's substantial submission to the Formless-Father over the cup. The cup-of-the-Father's-wrath the King about to drink, named in Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 51:17, 22; Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 25:15. The synoptic parallel at Matthew 26:39 carries the same Father-Son submission-substance.
cards.note: Matthew 26:39 — *And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.* *Saying, Father, if you be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but yours, be done.* (Luke 22:42) Matthew gives the same prayer in his own words. *O my Father, if it be possible*, let this cup pass, and then the turn, *not as I will, but as thou wilt*. Luke says it a little differently, but it is one prayer. The Son asks the Father, and the Son's will bends to the Father's.

cards.src_text: And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he says to his disciples, Sit you here, while I shall pray.
cards.tgt_text: Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of Yahuah (LORD) the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out.
cards.old_note: thread:gethsemane-cup-of-suffering-and-the-sons-substantial-submission-to-the-father | *Awake, awake, stand up, O Yerushalayim, which hast drunk at the hand of Yahuah the cup of his fury* (Yeshayahu/Isaiah 51:17, 22).
cards.note: Isaiah 51:17 — *Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of Yahuah (LORD) the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out.* *And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he says to his disciples, Sit you here, while I shall pray.* (Mark 14:32) Mark brings him to a place to pray, and Isaiah shows what weight the prayer carries. Jerusalem had drunk *the cup of his fury* from the hand of Yahuah (LORD) and wrung out the dregs of it. The cup is old and it is real, and it is the Father's.

cards.src_text: And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he says to his disciples, Sit you here, while I shall pray.
cards.tgt_text: For thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) unto me; Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it.
cards.old_note: thread:gethsemane-cup-of-suffering-and-the-sons-substantial-submission-to-the-father | Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 25:15-17's cup-of-wrath the Father hands the nations.
cards.note: Jeremiah 25:15 — *For thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) unto me; Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it.* *And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he says to his disciples, Sit you here, while I shall pray.* (Mark 14:32) Mark brings him to the place of prayer, and Jeremiah shows whose cup it is. Yahuah (LORD) hands the wine cup of fury to the prophet and sends him to carry it out. The cup is poured from the hand of Yahuah (LORD) and given to whom he chooses. That is the hand the Son looks to when he prays.

cards.member_note: Jeremiah 25:15 — *Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations.* The cup of fury is given out from the hand of Yahuah (LORD), so it is his to hand over.

cards.src_text: And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he says to his disciples, Sit you here, while I shall pray.
cards.tgt_text: Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;
cards.old_note: thread:gethsemane-cup-of-suffering-and-the-sons-substantial-submission-to-the-father | *The Formed Son's submission to the Formless Father walked out in the garden.* *Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears* (Hebrews 5:7-9).
cards.note: Hebrews 5:7 — *Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;* *And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he says to his disciples, Sit you here, while I shall pray.* (Mark 14:32) Hebrews says what the garden was. In the days of his flesh he offered prayers *with strong crying and tears* to the one able to save him from death, and he was heard. He asked, he feared, and he was heard. The Son at prayer in Mark's garden is the same Son who prayed this way.
cards.prose: Hebrews says what the garden was. In the days of his flesh he offered prayers *with strong crying and tears* to the one able to save him from death, and he was heard. He asked, he feared, and he was heard. The Son at prayer in Mark's garden is the same Son who prayed this way.

cards.src_text: Watch you and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.
cards.tgt_text: For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not.
cards.old_note: thread:gethsemane-cup-of-suffering-and-the-sons-substantial-submission-to-the-father | *The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.* The body-spirit asymmetry the disciple walks under (Romans 7:18-25). The watch-and-pray charge is not abolished by the cross; it is the disciple's standing rule.
cards.note: Romans 7:18 — *For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not.* *Watch you and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.* (Mark 14:38) He says the spirit is ready and the flesh is weak. Paul says the same weakness in his own words: to will is with him, but to do the good he finds not. The charge to watch and pray stands because the weakness stands. Paul also calls the law good in the same passage, so the weakness is in the flesh and not in the law.

cards.src_text: Watch you and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.
cards.tgt_text: For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would.
cards.old_note: thread:gethsemane-cup-of-suffering-and-the-sons-substantial-submission-to-the-father | *The flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh* (Galatians 5:17).
cards.note: Galatians 5:17 — *For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would.* *Watch you and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.* (Mark 14:38) Paul describes the same pull. The flesh wants one way and the Spirit another, and a man cannot do all he would. Yahusha (Jesus) said it to sleeping men in the garden and gave them the way through, *Watch ye and pray*. The weakness is plain, and so is the charge that goes with it.

cards.member_note: Galatians 5:17 — *the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh.* Paul describes the same pull between flesh and Spirit that Yahusha (Jesus) names when he finds the disciples asleep.

cards.tgt_text: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and Yahuah (LORD) hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.

cards.note: Isaiah 53:6 — *All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and Yahuah (LORD) hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.* *And he comes the third time, and says unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: it is enough, the hour is come; behold, the Son of Adam is betrayed into the hands of sinners.* (Mark 14:41) The hour has come and he is handed to sinners, and Isaiah had already said who laid it on him. *All we like sheep have gone astray*, each to his own way, and it was Yahuah (LORD) who laid the weight on him. cards.src_text: And immediately, while he yet spake, comes Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
cards.tgt_text: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.
cards.old_note: thread:gethsemane-cup-of-suffering-and-the-sons-substantial-submission-to-the-father | *The scriptures must be fulfilled.* Zecharyah (Zechariah) 13:7's smiting of the shepherd; the disciples scattering is the script the King quoted moments before.
cards.note: Zechariah 13:7 — *Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.* *And immediately, while he yet spake, comes Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.* (Mark 14:43) Judas comes with swords and staves, and Zechariah had already heard the order given. Yahuah (LORD) calls the sword against the shepherd, and the sheep are scattered. The crowd with its weapons is the sword the prophet saw. The scattered are *the little ones* his hand turns toward.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.
cards.tgt_text: And when Yahusha (Jesus) had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.
cards.old_note: thread:gethsemane-cup-of-suffering-and-the-sons-substantial-submission-to-the-father | *Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit* (Luke 23:46).
cards.note: Luke 23:46 — *And when Yahusha (Jesus) had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.* (Mark 15:37) Mark gives only the loud cry and the giving up of the ghost. Luke tells what the cry was: *Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit*. The last thing he does is what he did in the garden. He gives himself over to the Father.

cards.member_note: Luke 23:46 — *Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.* Luke gives the words of the loud cry, the spirit handed into the Father's hands.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.
cards.tgt_text: No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father.
cards.old_note: thread:gethsemane-cup-of-suffering-and-the-sons-substantial-submission-to-the-father | *Yahusha cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.* *No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself* (Yochanan/John 10:18).

This commandment have I received of my Father.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.* (Mark 15:37) He gave up the ghost, and John says no one took it from him. *I lay it down of myself*, he says, and he had the power to take it up again. It was a commandment from his Father. So the loud cry is a Son keeping a charge, not a man overpowered.
